description.from:
Outcome: Because a site is created by data with no human step, provisioning is an attack surface. Controls to build and review: (1) only a paid, verified Prospectus entitlement can trigger it, re-read from Prospectus before acting (never trust the event body); (2) per-Account and global rate limits on creation, learned from normal volume with an alarm (scan statistic), plus a hard stop the operator can flip; (3) validation of every input: site id and subdomain against the pattern and the reserved list, display names and starter text through the same moderation as public content, domains through ownership proof; (4) an append-only audit trail of every provisioning, lifecycle, domain and sign-in-client change (who, which Account, which tenant, what, when), kept outside the tenant's own data so deletion does not erase it; (5) the provisioning role can create tenant records but not read other tenants' content; (6) idempotent replay keys so a replayed event cannot create a second site; (7) abuse response: a created site can be taken offline in one command (PPY-d7c279). Output: threat model section, findings fixed or accepted in writing, before M7 opens provisioning to outside payers.

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): docs/security/shared-tier-threat-model.md (from PPY-3ff465), the provisioning function (PPY-70a429), Prospectus deployment routes (PPY-966ef5), the audit log store.

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/provisioning-controls.feature):
Scenario: A burst of site creations is stopped and reported
    Given one Account creates sites far above the learned rate
    When the next creation arrives
    Then it is held, the operator is alerted, and the audit trail records each attempt

Scenario: A forged provisioning event creates nothing
    Given an event naming an Account with no paid entitlement
    When provisioning re-reads the entitlement from Prospectus
    Then no tenant is created and the attempt is audited

Dependencies: blocked by PPY-966ef5, PPY-70a429. Blocks PPY-496c0b. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: -.

Testing: Review plus the Behave scenarios.
Rollout: Gate before M7 exits.
Risk and mitigation: Risk: the review happens after the API is in use. Mitigation: it blocks M7's exit, and provisioning stays operator-only until it passes.

Releasable on its own: not applicable (review gate).
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: unchanged.
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).

Joint review with Prospectus (2026-11-08). Prospectus's own review is kanbus-fa72e8; the two run together and share one threat model (docs/security/shared-tier-threat-model.md, PPY-3ff465). Inputs from kanbus-fa72e8 that Papyrus must answer or match: (1) who may create, change and delete a deployment (Papyrus shared-tier role, operators, later self-serve) and the abuse limits; (2) binding a shared-client token to one deployment so a token for tenant A cannot act on tenant B (host or audience checked centrally in authorize; Papyrus's pre-token Lambda issues claims only for the deployment authorize approved); (3) custom domain ownership proof, uniqueness across tenants, takeover after deletion (cooling-off before a hostname is released; Papyrus removes the edge host entry first); (4) storage, access and rotation of bring-your-own Google client secrets (decision D11); (5) replacing the per-site role list in the Prospectus API resource policy with one shared-tier Papyrus role; (6) Cyclotron lab verifier trust moving from the site registry to deployment records; (7) public-reader site subjects per deployment rather than per product; (8) deletion and export under billing standing; (9) every new IAM permission and parameter, for Ryan's approval.

Papyrus-side checks added: the provisioning role cannot read tenant content; the reconcile sweep and the event path share one idempotency key (deployment id plus revision); a retired deployment's tenant is suspended before its hostname is released; the audit trail lives outside tenant data and survives deletion.

Added scenario:
Scenario: A token for one deployment cannot act on another
    Given Ada is an admin of "alpha" and not a member of "beta"
    When she presents her alpha session to beta's newsroom or API
    Then authorize refuses it and no beta claim is issued
